quizzes.title: Kuki-Zomi and Meitei Tensions
quizzes.passage: Manipur has witnessed sharp tensions between Kuki-Zomi tribal groups and the Meitei community, and the violence that followed drew wide attention in the state. The conflict is set against a long history of differences over land, representation and administration. Meiteis form the largest population group in Manipur, while the hill areas cover most of the state's land. Hill communities have raised their own concerns, and different groups have sought political autonomy or separate administrative units. Court proceedings have also played a part in the sequence of events, as the Manipur High Court dealt with petitions connected to the community's status. The state government took several administrative actions during the period, including steps relating to armed groups and land-related disputes in the hills. Each of these decisions was received differently by the communities concerned, and the events were reported as a serious law and order crisis. The events placed heavy strain on relations between the groups living in the state. The episode also drew comment on the state's wider historical divisions. The disruption affected the daily life of people across the state, and the government faced sustained pressure to restore public confidence. The sequence of events was closely followed in the wider country, and it raised questions about how the state would manage its divided communities in the months ahead.

questions.q: Which community's demand for Scheduled Tribe status is listed among the immediate factors that triggered the violence?
questions.explanation: The Meitei community's demand for ST status, persisting since 2012, is listed as an immediate trigger of the violence.

questions.q: What did Kuki groups demand regarding Chief Minister Biren Singh?
questions.explanation: While the Meitei community backed Chief Minister Biren Singh, the Kukis demanded his resignation.

questions.q: On what ground did the state government evict 16 Kuki households?
questions.explanation: The state evicted 16 Kuki households over forest encroachment, which sparked protests from tribal groups.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Kuki groups opposed granting Scheduled Tribe status to the Meitei community.
Reason (R): Kukis feared that ST status would allow Meiteis to buy land in prohibited hill areas.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are supported, and the fear of land purchases in prohibited hill areas explains the Kuki opposition.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Meitei demand for ST status persisted since   ->   A. 1949 merger
II. Meiteis lost tribal status after   ->   B. 2012
III. Meitei Tribe Union petitioned   ->   C. March 2023
IV. Withdrawal from suspension of operations agreement   ->   D. High Court petition
questions.explanation: The demand persisted since 2012, tribal status was lost after the 1949 merger, the union petitioned the High Court, and the state withdrew from the agreement in March 2023.

questions.q:
Examine the statements below.
I. Violence between Kuki-Zomi tribals and the Meitei community was the first clash of its kind in three decades.
II. A 2023 High Court direction asked the state to consider a Meitei request for ST status.
III. The state government renewed its suspension of operations agreement with Kuki armed groups in March 2023.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the text, while statement III is wrong because the state withdrew from that agreement.

questions.q:
How many of the statements below are correct?
I. Violence erupted between Kuki-Zomi tribals and the Meitei community.
II. The Manipur government evicted Meitei households over forest encroachment.
III. The Meitei community backed Chief Minister Biren Singh during the crisis.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while statement II is wrong because the evicted households were Kuki.

quizzes.title: Kuki-Zomi and Meitei Violence Facts
quizzes.passage: Violence in Manipur has involved clashes between Kuki-Zomi tribal groups and the Meitei community, causing deep concern across the state. Disputes between these groups have roots in land, political representation and the status of communities. The Meitei community forms the majority of the state's population and mostly lives in the valley, while the hill areas have a larger share of land and fewer assembly seats. A demand for tribal recognition from the Meitei side has been pending for a long period and has been argued in the High Court. Kuki groups have voiced fears about how such recognition could affect land rights in hill areas. The state government has also taken actions including evictions linked to forest land, and the suspension of an operations agreement with armed groups was later withdrawn. These events came in a period of growing law and order concern, and the government of the day faced demands to step down. The situation shows how land, status and security concerns have become linked in the state's public life. Several of these developments were reported widely and shaped the debate on how the state should respond to the violence. The episode drew national attention to the state's recent politics.

questions.q: Since which year has the Meitei demand for Scheduled Tribe status persisted?
questions.explanation: The Meitei demand for ST status has persisted since 2012, according to the booklet.

questions.q: How many Kuki households were evicted over forest encroachment?
questions.explanation: The state government evicted 16 Kuki households over forest encroachment.

questions.q: Which two armed groups' suspension of operations agreement did the state withdraw from in March 2023? (names)
questions.answer: Kuki National Army and Zomi Revolutionary Army
accept: Kuki National Army and Zomi Revolutionary Army
Kuki National Army, Zomi Revolutionary Army
questions.explanation: The state withdrew from the suspension of operations agreement with the Kuki National Army and the Zomi Revolutionary Army in March 2023.

questions.q: The first clash of its kind in Manipur came after how many decades? (number)
questions.explanation: The violence was the first clash of this kind in three decades in Manipur.

questions.q: In which year did the Meitei community lose its tribal status through a merger?
questions.explanation: The Meitei community's tribal status was lost after the 1949 merger.

questions.q: Which Chief Minister did the Meitei community back while Kuki groups demanded resignation? (name)
questions.explanation: The Meitei community backed Chief Minister N. Biren Singh while the Kukis demanded his resignation.

questions.q: Which union petitioned the Manipur High Court seeking recognition of tribal status for the Meitei community? (name)
questions.explanation: The Meitei Tribe Union petitioned the Manipur High Court for recognition of tribal status.

quizzes.title: Manipur's Long-Standing Divides
quizzes.passage: Manipur's social and political life is shaped by a set of long-standing divides. Its population is not spread evenly across the state's landscape, and the differences between its plains and its hills have affected how land and political representation are organised. Communities have different rights when it comes to property, and these rules have been points of debate over decades. Political representation has also been contested, with hill communities raising concerns about how seats are distributed in the legislature. Census data and the drawing of constituency boundaries have drawn attention from several groups, and the state's external border has added to security concerns in recent years. Several groups have also raised questions about how their identities and cultural ways of life can be protected. The state's constitutional history includes several stages of change, and its institutions have developed through those stages. Public debate on these matters continues in the state's assembly and in the wider press. Such debates have a history that goes back many years. The Manipur High Court, Parliament and the state government have all been involved in such questions at different times. Political debates on these questions have shaped the state's public life for a long time. These issues remain central to the way its politics is understood.

questions.q: What percentage of Manipur's population is made up of Meiteis?
questions.explanation: Meiteis comprise 52 per cent of Manipur's population.

questions.q: Where can tribal communities buy land, a right that Meiteis do not have across most of the state?
questions.explanation: Tribals can buy land in the Imphal Valley, while Meiteis are restricted from buying land in about 90 per cent of Manipur.

questions.q: Which Act is described as giving extensive powers to the military in affected regions?
questions.explanation: The booklet describes the Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act as granting extensive powers to the military, linked to allegations of human rights abuses.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Meitei community has concerns about the delimitation process in Manipur.
Reason (R): The Meitei community questions the accuracy of census figures from 2020.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both are stated, and the doubts about the 2020 census figures underlie the concerns about delimitation.

questions.q:

I. Rapid growth of villages in Churachandpur   ->   C. Drug trafficking and cross-border crime

III. Proximity to Golden Triangle and porous borders   ->   A. Migrant influx

questions.q:
Examine the statements below.
I. Hill areas cover most of Manipur's land.
II. Hill areas hold 40 of the 60 assembly seats.
III. Tribal communities can buy land in the Imphal Valley.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II is wrong because hill areas hold only 20 of the 60 seats.

questions.q:
How many of the statements below are correct?
I. Meiteis live mainly in the valley areas of Manipur.
II. Meiteis can buy land in every part of Manipur.
III. Imphal is the capital of Manipur.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while statement II is wrong because Meiteis are restricted from buying land in much of the state.

quizzes.title: Manipur Geography and Land Facts
quizzes.passage: Manipur's history includes a formal union with India after a period of separate rule. Its landscape is divided between a populous plain and large upland tracts, and this geography shapes how land can be owned and how seats are allotted in the legislature. Different communities face different restrictions on land purchase, depending on where they live. Groups in the hills have criticised the distribution of seats, while groups in the valley have raised concerns about the figures used for population counts and boundary drawing. Border issues and cross-border movement add a security dimension, as the state sits next to a neighbouring country that has seen political upheaval. Trafficking and criminal networks have also been a worry in the region, given the state's location. The combination of these factors has made Manipur's politics complex, with each issue linked to questions of identity, representation and security. These patterns were visible long before recent events and continue to affect discussions about governance. Each of these issues is discussed in the context of the state's population and geography. The state's public life reflects these questions in many forms. The state government and the courts have each been involved in responding to these questions. Such matters continue to be debated in the state.

questions.q: In which year did Manipur's ruler sign the Treaty of Accession that merged Manipur into India? (year)
questions.explanation: The Maharaja signed the treaty merging Manipur into India in 1947.

questions.q: How many of the 60 assembly seats do the hill areas hold? (number)
questions.explanation: The hill areas have only 20 of the 60 assembly seats.

questions.q: What percentage of Manipur's land do the hill areas cover? (number)
questions.explanation: The hill areas cover 89 per cent of the state's land.

questions.q: In what percentage of Manipur are Meiteis restricted from buying land? (number)
questions.explanation: Meiteis are restricted from buying land in 90 per cent of Manipur.

questions.q: Which neighbouring country's coup triggered a refugee crisis in India's North-East? (name)
questions.explanation: The Myanmar coup triggered a refugee crisis in India's North-East.

questions.q: Which two groups demand greater political autonomy or separate administrative units? (names)
questions.explanation: The Nagas and Kukis demand greater political autonomy or separate administrative units.

questions.q: Manipur's proximity to which region increases its vulnerability to drug trafficking? (name)
questions.explanation: Manipur's proximity to the Golden Triangle and its porous borders increase vulnerability to drug trafficking.

quizzes.title: Records of President's Rule
quizzes.passage: Indian states have sometimes been placed under direct central control when their elected governments cannot run the administration in line with the Constitution. This arrangement is commonly called by a name that refers to the President, and it sits within a wider framework of constitutional emergency provisions. The history of this arrangement reaches back to the early years after independence, when Punjab, PEPSU and Andhra were among the first units brought under it. The records of the later instances show wide differences in how often and for how long each state remained under it. Over time the power drew sustained attention from the courts, and questions about how far the central government could go in using it became part of legal debate. The Constitution sets out the procedure for placing a state under such control, the approval needed from Parliament, and the period for which the arrangement can run. Manipur is among the states that have experienced this arrangement several times. Its political history is therefore closely tied to the repeated use of this power, and the issue remains a subject of constitutional discussion in the state and at the national level. Each instance is recorded separately, with its own dates and duration. The records are useful for comparing one instance with another.

questions.q: Under which Article can the President issue a proclamation when a State Government cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 356 empowers the President to issue a proclamation when a state government cannot be carried on per the Constitution.

questions.q: Till Parliament approves a proclamation, what can the President do with the State Legislative Assembly?
questions.explanation: Till Parliament approves, the President can only suspend the Legislative Assembly.

questions.q: Who can declare that the powers of the State Legislature are to be exercised by Parliament?
questions.explanation: The President can declare that the powers of the State Legislature are to be exercised by Parliament.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A proclamation revoking President's Rule does not need parliamentary approval.
Reason (R): Parliamentary approval is required for every revocation of President's Rule.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: A is true because a revocation needs only a subsequent proclamation, so R, which says approval is required, is false.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Punjab (first instance)   ->   D. 1953
II. PEPSU (first instance)   ->   A. 1975
III. Andhra (first instance)   ->   B. 1951
IV. 38th Amendment Act   ->   C. 1954
questions.explanation: Punjab was 1951, PEPSU 1953, Andhra 1954, and the 38th Amendment Act was 1975.

questions.q:
Examine the statements below.
I. A resolution approving a proclamation can be passed by a simple majority in either House.
II. The proclamation of President's Rule is issued by Parliament, not by the President.
III. Under President's Rule, the President can take up the functions of the State Government.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II is wrong because the President issues the proclamation.

questions.q:
How many of the statements below are correct?
I. President's Rule is popularly known as State Emergency.
II. Manipur was the first state placed under President's Rule.
III. The President can revoke a proclamation only after both Houses approve it.
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since Punjab was first and revocation needs no parliamentary approval.

quizzes.title: Early Instances and Judicial Points
quizzes.passage: A state's elected government may fail to run its administration in line with the Constitution. When that happens, the Union can take direct control of the state, and the arrangement is widely discussed in India under a name tied to the head of the Union. The power is connected to the Centre's responsibility to see that every state is governed according to the Constitution. Its use has a long record, and the first instances in the country date to the early period after independence. Such records show that the length of each instance has differed from one state to another. The power has also been examined by courts, which have looked at how far the central action can go. Legal debates have addressed the scope of the Centre's power, the steps needed for parliamentary involvement, and the powers that remain with the state legislature during the period. The Constitution sets out the procedure for the arrangement, including how a proclamation is approved and how long it can last. Manipur has experienced this arrangement more than once, which has made the topic a recurring subject in the state's political history. The records of each instance include the dates on which the arrangement began.

questions.q: In which year was President's Rule first imposed in Punjab? (year)
questions.explanation: Punjab was the first of the early instances, in 1951.

questions.q: Which state had President's Rule in 1953 among the first three instances? (name)
questions.explanation: PEPSU's President's Rule came in 1953, the second of the first three instances.

questions.q: Which Amendment Act of 1975 made the President's satisfaction final and not challengeable in any court? (name)
questions.explanation: The 38th Amendment Act of 1975 made the President's satisfaction final and not challengeable in any court.

questions.q: Besides 'President's Rule', what is the popular name for this arrangement? (two words)
questions.explanation: The arrangement is also popularly known as State Emergency.

questions.q: In which year was President's Rule first imposed in Andhra, the third of the first three instances? (year)
questions.explanation: Andhra's President's Rule came in 1954, the third of the first three instances.

questions.q: Until Parliament approves a proclamation, what is the only power the President has over the Legislative Assembly? (one word)
questions.explanation: Till Parliament approves, the President can only suspend the Legislative Assembly.

questions.q: What majority is required for a resolution approving President's Rule in either House? (two words)
questions.explanation: A resolution approving President's Rule is passed by a simple majority of members present and voting.
